raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Extends the NVIDIA megakernel plugin contract to cover prefill and extend steps, in addition to decode. Today the plugin interface handles `target_verify` and `draft_extend` (inside CUDA graphs) but not regular target prefill/extend. This PR adds the framework-side contract so a plugin spec in `sgl-nvidia-mega` can implement a prefill megakernel through the same interface.

Discussed with the SGL team — see linked thread. Yangmin Li confirmed the current interface does not cover regular prefill/extend and a new mode is needed. This PR provides that mode; the in-tree consumer is a separate PR in `sgl-nvidia-mega`.

## Modifications

- **`Requirements.prefill_graph_backends`** (empty by default): a decode-only spec is unaffected on every path. When non-empty, SGLang checks the prefill graph backend at startup and installs a prefill capture-check hook.
- **`BuildContext.prefill_widths`**: the captured prefill graph token buckets, passed to the spec's `build`. Empty for decode-only specs or when prefill graphs are off.
- **`Step.mode`** may now be `"extend"` (a prefill/extend step), in addition to `"decode"` and `"target_verify"`.
- **`_Dispatch.captured_tokens`**: tracks which prefill token buckets ran the megakernel during capture (decode still uses `captured` keyed by batch size).
- **`_CaptureCheck`** now accepts a `phase` argument (`"decode"` or `"prefill"`). A prefill instance is installed only for a spec that declares `prefill_graph_backends`, so decode-only specs are refused on their decode graphs alone and never asked to run a prefill graph they never claimed.
- **`ModelRunner.prefill_capture_tail_hooks`**: separate list for the prefill graph runner, so decode capture hooks are never handed a prefill capture.
- **`PrefillCudaGraphRunner`**: calls `prefill_capture_tail_hooks` after each graph capture, with the same contract as the decode runner's `capture_tail_hooks`.

## Tests

- `test_megakernel_guards.py`: new test verifying that only a spec declaring `prefill_graph_backends` is checked on the prefill graph backend, and that a decode-only spec is unaffected.
- `test_megakernel_runtime.py`: new test verifying that a prefill-covering spec receives `prefill_widths`, gets a prefill `_CaptureCheck`, the check is keyed by token bucket (not batch size), and the check refuses when no prefill graph runs the megakernel.
- Both tests run on CPU.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (no serving path change; contract-only extension with CPU tests).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

This new test fails at the head commit. `install_megakernel` checks requirements through `_requirement_reasons` (binding.py:1437), which checks `decode_graph_backends` but not the new `prefill_graph_backends`. So installing `PREFILL` with prefill graphs `disabled` raises nothing, and the test fails with "ValueError not raised". I reproduced this on CPU with `pytest test_megakernel_runtime.py`.

**Why it matters**

Argument resolution (`megakernel_disable_reasons`) checks only the target's spec. A draft spec is checked only in `_requirement_reasons`, so a draft spec that declares `prefill_graph_backends` is never held to them.

**Fix**

Add a prefill backend check to `_requirement_reasons`, next to the decode check. With that change, this test passes locally. Also add `prefill_graph_backends` to the load-time list in the `MegakernelSpec` docstring.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`forward` writes every captured step into both `captured` (by batch size) and `captured_tokens` (by token count). `capture_cuda_graphs` captures prefill graphs before decode graphs, so the decode `_CaptureCheck` also sees prefill steps. A breakable prefill capture has `batch_size == 1`, so its `extend` step lands in `captured[1]`.

**Example**

Use the `PREFILL` spec with prefill buckets `[2, 8]`, then capture decode `capture_bs=[5, 6]`, which the spec does not cover. The decode check does not refuse. It logs "runs the decode graphs of batch sizes [1] (1 of 3)", but no decode graph of batch size 1 exists.

**Fix**

Write one dict per capture: `captured_tokens` when `forward_batch.forward_mode == ForwardMode.EXTEND`, else `captured`. Add a test that captures prefill, then decode, on one dispatch.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

An `extend` step still gets the decode-only view on the hybrid MLA/KDA binding. `_Dispatch.forward` calls `MegakernelBinding.forward_view`, and `_hybrid_step` reads `full_backend.forward_decode_metadata`. `TRTLLMMLABackend` sets only `forward_prefill_metadata` for an EXTEND batch, so the view holds stale decode metadata or raises "MLA decode metadata is unavailable".

`seal_capture_view` also keys its seals by `mode:batch_size`. Breakable prefill buckets all have batch size 1, so the second bucket fails with "was reallocated after its first read".

**Fix**

Until the binding has an extend view, make `_hybrid_step` raise a clear error for an EXTEND batch. Or state in this `Step.mode` contract that `extend` is not supported on hybrid MLA/KDA models.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

SGLang passes `prefill_widths` to `build`, but `BuiltMegakernel` has no field for the prefill widths it actually built. So `install_megakernel` cannot run `megakernel_agree` on them, as it does for `built.widths` (binding.py:1232). That decode check exists because ranks that build different widths wait in different collectives.

**Example**

On TP 4, rank 0 builds prefill buckets `(2, 8)` and rank 1 builds only `(2,)`. At an 8-token prefill, rank 0 runs the megakernel and rank 1 runs the standard forward, so the ranks hang.

**Fix**

Add a built prefill-widths field to `BuiltMegakernel`. Read it only for a spec that declares `prefill_graph_backends`, agree it across ranks next to the decode widths, and refuse such a spec when it built none.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`_expected` uses `getattr(runner, "capture_bs", None)` and `getattr(runner, "capture_num_tokens", None)`. Both runners always set these fields, so `getattr` only hides errors. If a field is renamed, `expected` becomes `None`, the check returns early on every call, and a runner that never runs the megakernel is never refused.

**Fix**

Type the runner and read the fields directly:

```python
def _expected(
    self, runner: Union[DecodeCudaGraphRunner, PrefillCudaGraphRunner]
) -> Collection[int]:
    if self.phase == Phase.DECODE:
        return runner.capture_bs
    return runner.capture_num_tokens
```

Then drop the `expected is None` check in `__call__`.

**Blocking.** With `breakable` and `full` prefill graphs, `PrefillCudaGraphRunner._run_forward` captures `self.layer_model.forward` (the transformer body, prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:944-962), not the outer `model.forward` that `_Dispatch` wraps. So `plan()` never runs inside a prefill capture, `captured_tokens` stays empty, and this check never reaches a verdict: it neither logs nor refuses. At replay, `_execute_body_capture` calls the outer `model.forward` eagerly (prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:2335-2377), so a spec whose `plan()` returns an `extend` step runs eagerly there and skips the captured body unless it calls `original`.

Would it make sense to state which path an extend step is meant to take? One option is to keep `extend` eager-only for now (accept only `disabled` prefill graphs and drop `prefill_widths` and the prefill check until a capture path exists); another is to define the replaced segment as the transformer body these runners capture. A test that follows `capture_one_shape`'s real call order would catch this.

nodes.body:
**Suggestion.** For `decode` and `target_verify`, the bindings hand the plugin frozen step views (`HybridStepView`, `EagleForwardView`) and list what it may write. `extend` adds no such view, so a plugin would read prefix lengths, extend lengths and state indices directly from `ForwardBatch` and the backend's `forward_metadata`. Would it make sense to define an extend step view here (prefix and extend lengths, write slots, KV and state indices), and to state what an extend step may write (only the KV at `out_cache_loc`, or also linear-attention state)? It would also help to say how a `MIXED` batch and a chunk with a cached prefix are classified: the prefill runner replays `MIXED` as `EXTEND` (prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:2073-2082), while the eager path passes `MIXED` through.

Could you also link the sgl-nvidia-mega PR that consumes `extend`? It would show what the plugin reads in an extend step.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

repo.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.
repo.name: sglang

detail.body:
## Motivation

Extends the NVIDIA megakernel plugin contract to cover prefill and extend steps, in addition to decode. Today the plugin interface handles `target_verify` and `draft_extend` (inside CUDA graphs) but not regular target prefill/extend. This PR adds the framework-side contract so a plugin spec in `sgl-nvidia-mega` can implement a prefill megakernel through the same interface.

Discussed with the SGL team — see linked thread. Yangmin Li confirmed the current interface does not cover regular prefill/extend and a new mode is needed. This PR provides that mode; the in-tree consumer is a separate PR in `sgl-nvidia-mega`.

## Modifications

- **`Requirements.prefill_graph_backends`** (empty by default): a decode-only spec is unaffected on every path. When non-empty, SGLang checks the prefill graph backend at startup and installs a prefill capture-check hook.
- **`BuildContext.prefill_widths`**: the captured prefill graph token buckets, passed to the spec's `build`. Empty for decode-only specs or when prefill graphs are off.
- **`Step.mode`** may now be `"extend"` (a prefill/extend step), in addition to `"decode"` and `"target_verify"`.
- **`_Dispatch.captured_tokens`**: tracks which prefill token buckets ran the megakernel during capture (decode still uses `captured` keyed by batch size).
- **`_CaptureCheck`** now accepts a `phase` argument (`"decode"` or `"prefill"`). A prefill instance is installed only for a spec that declares `prefill_graph_backends`, so decode-only specs are refused on their decode graphs alone and never asked to run a prefill graph they never claimed.
- **`ModelRunner.prefill_capture_tail_hooks`**: separate list for the prefill graph runner, so decode capture hooks are never handed a prefill capture.
- **`PrefillCudaGraphRunner`**: calls `prefill_capture_tail_hooks` after each graph capture, with the same contract as the decode runner's `capture_tail_hooks`.

## Tests

- `test_megakernel_guards.py`: new test verifying that only a spec declaring `prefill_graph_backends` is checked on the prefill graph backend, and that a decode-only spec is unaffected.
- `test_megakernel_runtime.py`: new test verifying that a prefill-covering spec receives `prefill_widths`, gets a prefill `_CaptureCheck`, the check is keyed by token bucket (not batch size), and the check refuses when no prefill graph runs the megakernel.
- Both tests run on CPU.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (no serving path change; contract-only extension with CPU tests).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

This new test fails at the head commit. `install_megakernel` checks requirements through `_requirement_reasons` (binding.py:1437), which checks `decode_graph_backends` but not the new `prefill_graph_backends`. Would it make sense for each binding to declare the step modes it serves, and for `install_megakernel` to refuse a spec with `prefill_graph_backends` on a binding that does not serve `extend`? That would turn a capture- or replay-time error into a startup refusal.

inline_comments.body:
**Suggestion.** For `decode` and `target_verify`, the bindings hand the plugin frozen step views (`HybridStepView`, `EagleForwardView`) and list what it may write. `extend` adds no such view, so a plugin would read prefix lengths, extend lengths and state indices directly from `ForwardBatch` and the backend's `forward_metadata`. Would it make sense to define an extend step view here (prefix and extend lengths, write slots, KV and state indices), and to state what an extend step may write (only the KV at `out_cache_loc`, or also linear-attention state)? It would also help to say how a `MIXED` batch and a chunk with a cached prefix are classified: the prefill runner replays `MIXED` as `EXTEND` (prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py:2073-2082), while the eager path passes `MIXED` through.

Could you also link the sgl-nvidia-mega PR that consumes `extend`? It would show what the plugin reads in an extend step.
